historical_commentary.text: This note presents a technique for storing user-editable pick lists (and multi-value keyword tags) in a database table rather than in the structure file, so list edits survive structure updates, implemented via a single dispatching Project Method and inter-process arrays loaded at startup, an approach the author explicitly frames as a 2004-era redesign of a similar 2000-era Technical Note. The core problem it solves — persisting user-editable lists independent of structure/schema changes — is timeless and still relevant to any database application, but the specific implementation idioms (raw hierarchical lists, inter-process arrays, structure-file separation from data file) are classic 4D Design Mode patterns that a modern 4D developer would likely implement differently using current list-box/collection-based UI objects and ORDA-style data access.
related_updates: 4D has since introduced richer list-box and collection-based UI objects that can implement similar user-editable list functionality with less custom code
ORDA (introduced in 4D v17, 2018) offers a more modern data-access approach than the raw table/inter-process-array pattern shown here
The general problem (persisting editable lists independent of structure changes) remains a common and valid concern in current 4D development
